# President announces new sanctions targeting Russia's defense industry and financial networks

Ukraine is preparing new sanctions packages targeting Russia's defense industry, financial networks and intermediaries that facilitate the production of missiles and drones and contribute to prolonging the war.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said this in his nightly [video address](https://www.president.gov.ua/en/news/zavdyaki-vsim-rishennyam-vid-minuloyi-oseni-mi-zmogli-zimoyu-105833), according to Ukrinform.

"Our sanctions against Russian oil refineries and other facilities in Russia's oil sector, our mid-range strikes against Russian military logistics, and our operation in the waters of the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov – all of this is working to limit Russia's war potential. It is important to continue this with more active political and legal measures as well," he said.

He recalled that Ukraine had imposed a sanctions package today targeting companies and vessels involved in exporting grain and other goods stolen in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine.

"We are preparing new sanctions packages against Russia's war industry, financial chains, and intermediaries. Unfortunately, a significant number of Russian enterprises working for the war are still not under international sanctions, and this must be corrected during August and September. We will raise this with leaders at all working levels," Zelensky said.

# Russia won’t accept a new Black Sea truce, saying the West already broke its word once

Source: [Meduza](https://meduza.io/feature/2026/08/14/voyna)

Wheat being loaded at a farm in Ukraine’s Zhytomyr region, August 7, 2026

Valentyn Ogirenko / Reuters / Scanpix / LETA

Moscow has not received a formal proposal for a moratorium on Black Sea strikes, Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova [said](https://t.me/MariaVladimirovnaZakharova/13651) on Friday. A day earlier, Reuters [reported](https://meduza.io/news/2026/08/13/reuters-ukraina-predlozhila-rossii-peremirie-v-chernom-more) that Kyiv had used an intermediary to deliver a proposal to Moscow for a mutual halt to strikes on civilian targets in the Black Sea. Reuters did not name the intermediary directly, but it was likely Turkey — Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan had already [said](https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/8875625) on August 8 that Ankara had sent a moratorium proposal to both sides in the conflict.

“The Russian side has not received, through official channels, any formal communication from Turkey setting out the terms of this initiative,” Zakharova said.

Moscow does not see “grounds for half-measures that only give the Kyiv regime a temporary reprieve,” she said. Russia agreed to a moratorium in 2022–2023 in exchange for access to global markets for its agricultural products, she said, but “the West acted in bad faith” and did not lift sanctions.
